title: Choose the visual world for Kube UI
question: The roll assigned Airport Wayfinding. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Airport Wayfinding
options.lineage: Aicher-school airport sign systems (Frankfurt, Munich, Schiphol)
options.thesis: Every screen answers 'where am I and what changed' the way a concourse sign does.
options.viewport: Graphite shell; the active cluster tab, nav item, selected row and live log tab carry the one yellow band; pods table dense with tabular figures; drawer right, logs bottom.
options.risk: Yellow must stay reserved for 'you are here'; spend it on decoration and the system collapses.

raised.raise: Change board: a row whose status, ready or restarts changed lights a held marker until you look at it, like a gate change that stays lit.
Hierarchy by scale and weight alone: no cards or boxes to rank content.
One fixed lifecycle vocabulary (pending, creating, running, terminating, failed) drawn identically in tables, drawer, chips and tabs.
Restarts on a fixed severity ramp: none, outlined amber, filled red at five or more.

options.label: Transit Line Map
options.lineage: metro line diagrams and line-coloured station signage (BTS, Tokyo Metro)
options.thesis: Namespaces and pods are lines with their own colours, so a merged log reads like a line map.
options.viewport: Light ground; cluster tabs as line badges; each namespace a coloured line down the table's edge; pods as station dots; log lines tagged with their pod's line colour.
options.risk: Many namespaces at once exhaust distinguishable line colours; this is also a familiar dev-tool pastel look when set timidly.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: boarding pass and live departure board
options.thesis: Pods ranked like departures; a changed row moves, flashes its alert colour and holds it until noticed.
options.viewport: Light board; pods ordered by most recent change; drawer as a segmented pass with labelled fields.
options.case: Wins product clarity for an all-day glanced screen; loses audience identification to signage.
options.risk: Re-ranking rows by change fights the stable alphabetical order you rely on to find a pod.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.thesis: The whole shell is a yellow sign band; content hangs beneath it in black and white.
options.viewport: Yellow top band with black cluster tabs and pickers; black nav rail with white pictograms; white content table.
options.case: Same world as the roll, committed harder; loses on calm for a screen open all day.
options.risk: A yellow band in view all day is loud on a second screen.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Hierarchy by scale contrast on a strict baseline grid.
options.viewport: Giant specimen letter over a glyph grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in a pod list wants display type.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale and weight alone.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the whole screen.
options.viewport: One item per screen with a right rail of actions.
options.case: Fuses poorly: this job needs many rows at once.
options.kept: Actions live on one rail beside the content, never inside it.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One subject through fixed life stages at a fixed scale.
options.viewport: Five aligned plates of one plant.
options.case: Fuses poorly: cream and italic serif read as a book, not a cluster tool.
options.kept: One fixed lifecycle state vocabulary used everywhere.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Importance as mark size on a fixed magnitude ramp.
options.viewport: A chart of ranked dots on a coordinate grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a map metaphor has no place in tables of pods.
options.kept: A fixed severity ramp for restarts.
options.risk: Pretty but unreadable for row data.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark developer tool in the Lens / Linear manner, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement you have now, rebuilt with full craft and custom controls.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dev tool by design.
